topic: low-band calibration improvement and band-limiting feasibility
motivation: band-limiting the forward path to 300-3400 Hz removes the 8.4 kHz resonance from the loop (|F*H| there drops to -35.75 dB) but the limiting point had already moved to 381-435 Hz inside the band, so the forward filter buys almost nothing for the cancellation arm. The real lever is 300-1000 Hz cancellation quality, where coherence was only 0.81.

bandpass_300_3400_order6.note: 8.2-8.6 kHz loop term falls to -35.75 dB but the limiting bin is 381 Hz

board_verification.protocol: loop only, source off, 3 s per trial, two repeats per gain, no 1.5 dB gate

results.+3 dB: held 1/2, the howling repeat reached -1.7 dBFS peak
results.main_frequency: 9131 Hz in three of four trials, 457 Hz in the howling one

agreement: the predicted limit (+5.42 dB from max|H-Hhat|) matches the observed threshold of +3 to +5 dB, so the metric is usable as a design target
gain_over_previous: the deployed model howled at -3 dB in one session; this one holds at 0 dB and is borderline at +3 dB, about 6 dB better
remaining_gap: a usable PA needs roughly +20 dB; the canceller now gives about +5 dB, so about 15 dB are still missing
